raw_response:
I will still do wheat-maize on all 12 mu, because that is what fits my land and water, and I know how to manage it. I have well irrigation, so I will not farm too lightly on fertilizer. Wheat needs a steady stand through winter and a push in spring, and maize needs enough base fertilizer plus topdressing after it gets tall. I went to middle school, so I do not just copy blindly, but I still look at what nearby farmers do. Around here, if fertilizer is too low, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on inputs. My farm is 12 mu, not tiny, so I can put in enough fertilizer but still have to watch costs because some money also has to go to sprays and field work. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, keep rotary tillage because it is quicker and cheaper for me, irrigate wheat more times than maize, and plan my pesticide sprays around the usual weeds, aphids, rust, and corn borers. I will aim for a stable harvest first, not gamble on cutting inputs too hard.
